source.section: Form NJ-1040 lines 15, 20a, 27, 28a, 29: Instr PDF p.22 line 28a chart column $125,001-$150,000 ('18.75% of line 20a'), PDF p.16 IRA withdrawals, PDF p.21 line 27, PDF p.23 Worksheet D; GIT-1 & 2 p.19; PDF p.8 lines 6-7 (regular and senior 65+ exemptions), PDF p.9 line 13, PDF p.25 line 30, PDF p.27 lines 38-39, PDF p.33 lines 42-43, PDF p.65 Tax Rate Schedules

worked: Federal AGI 130,000.00 (wages 66,000.00 + private pension 44,000.00 + IRA distribution 20,000.00); federal taxable income = 130,000.00 - 17,750.00 federal standard deduction (15,750 single + 2,000 for age 65 or older) = 112,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Line 15 wages 66,000.00 + line 20a pension and IRA 64,000.00 = line 27 total income 130,000.00; measure 130,000.00, in the 125,001-150,000 band, single share 0.1875. Line 28a: age 65; Line A = 64,000.00, Line B = 18.75% x 64,000.00 = 12,000.00; lesser = 12,000.00. Projection: 0.1875 x lesser of (64,000.00, cap 75,000.00) = 12,000.00. Line 28b: wages 66,000 are more than 3,000, so no unclaimed exclusion; projection 0.00 (no covered interest, dividends or gains). Line 29 New Jersey gross income = 130,000.00 - 12,000.00 - 0.00 = 118,000.00. Line 30 exemptions (line 13): regular 1,000 x 1 + senior 65+ 1,000 x 1 = 2,000.00; line 38 = 2,000.00 (no other deductions). Line 39/42 taxable income = 118,000.00 - 2,000.00 = 116,000.00. Line 43 tax, rate schedule Table A (single/separate) as bands: 20,000.00 x 0.014 = 280.00 + 15,000.00 x 0.0175 = 262.50 + 5,000.00 x 0.035 = 175.00 + 35,000.00 x 0.05525 = 1,933.75 + 41,000.00 x 0.0637 = 2,611.70 = 5,262.95. No credits. State income tax = 5,262.95. The pension is noncontributory, so the New Jersey taxable amount (line 20a) equals the federal taxable amount and line 20b is empty. The IRA was funded only by a rollover from a 401(k) (pre-tax in New Jersey too), so it has no New Jersey basis and Worksheet C gives no excludable part. Taxable income is 100,000 or more, so the booklet itself uses the rate schedule.
